extracted.intended_audience: NSF grant applicants, awardees, institutional research administrators, and NSF program and grants staff
extracted.subtask_description: Supplemental policy notice implementing revisions to the NSF Proposal & Award Policies and Procedures Guide (PAPPG 24-1), effective Dec 8, 2025, covering proposal types, eligibility, allowable costs, data management, review procedures, financial/reporting requirements, research security, property management, and research integrity/misconduct definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability and Precedence of Notice
rubrics_metrics.description: This notice takes precedence over existing policies and procedures in PAPPG 24-1 and applies to all financial assistance awarded on or after Dec. 8, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to NSF grants and cooperative agreements; supplements and supersedes provisions in the 24-1 PAPPG for awards on/after the effective date. See publication NSF 26-200.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR Project Pitch submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduces 'Project Pitch' as a new proposal type for NSF SBIR/STTR: the Project Pitch is the first step and proposers must receive an official invitation via the Project Pitch process to submit an SBIR/STTR Phase I or Fast-Track proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small businesses may submit one Project Pitch per submission deadline (refer to current SBIR/STTR Phase I or Fast-Track solicitation). Project Pitches will be internally reviewed by a member of the SBIR/STTR team. See program website (https://seedfund.nsf.gov/apply/project-pitch) for submission instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal organization terminology and definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarifies terminology by defining 'Indian Tribe' (formerly 'Tribal Nations') to mean an American Indian or Alaska Native tribe, band, nation, pueblo, village, or community acknowledged as federally recognized by the Secretary of the Interior per the Federally Recognized Indian Tribe List Act of 1994; includes Alaska Native village or regional or village-corporation as defined under the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replaces prior 'Tribal Nations' wording to improve clarity and more thoroughly cover Native-owned lands and entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposer limitations regarding Confucius Institutes
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with Section 10339A of the CHIPS and Science Act of 2022 (42 U.S.C. § 19039), NSF funds may not be awarded to an Institution of Higher Education (IHE) that maintains a contract or agreement with a Confucius Institute unless specifically approved by a waiver from the NSF Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementing statutory restriction; see NSF Important Notice 149 (section 6) for related research security policy updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable and unallowable costs — American Security Drone Act compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits use of NSF funds on or after Dec. 22, 2025 to procure unmanned aircraft systems (drones) manufactured or assembled by a covered foreign entity or to use NSF funds in connection with operation of such drones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibited sources include entities on the Consolidated Screening List and entities from the People’s Republic of China or subject to PRC influence/control as determined by DHS; cross-reference provided to Consolidated Screening List and GSA resources (smartpay link).

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Management and Sharing Plans — Gold Standard Science alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are required to share all data supporting NSF-funded publications at the time of publication; any exceptions to sharing must be described and justified within the Data Management and Sharing Plan (DMSP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implements public access requirements aligned with NSF's Gold Standard Science Implementation Plan and OSTP guidance. Directorates/units may have specific DMSP requirements at www.nsf.gov/public-access. Emphasis on reproducibility and transparency; justification required for access limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal-specific funding threshold increases (Planning, RAPID, EAGER)
rubrics_metrics.description: Updates funding request caps: Planning proposals up to $200,000 per year (previously $100,000) for up to two years; RAPID proposals up to $300,000 (previously $200,000) including indirect costs for up to one year; EAGER proposals up to $400,000 (previously $300,000) including indirect costs for up to two years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award size should be consistent with scope of proposed activities and comparable to planning grants in similar areas; language replaces prior numeric caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum number of reviewers for full proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Full proposals, unless excepted, must be reviewed by at least two reviewers; one or more of those reviews may be conducted internally by NSF staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF guidelines for reviewer selection are designed to ensure selection of experts who can provide Program Officers with proper information to recommend in accordance with NSB-approved criteria. (Text notes 'Optimally, reviewers should have…' indicating additional guidance on reviewer expertise.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal not accepted or returned without review — responsiveness and sufficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposal will be returned without review if it is not responsive to the NSF funding opportunity or does not contain sufficient content to permit effective merit review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies grounds for returning proposals without review; proposals must contain sufficient detail to enable meaningful merit evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR Phase II reconsiderations removed
rubrics_metrics.description: Reconsideration for SBIR/STTR proposals (Phase I and related) has been removed; the provision for reconsideration for SBIR/STTR proposals is eliminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implements administrative change removing reconsideration pathway for SBIR/STTR proposals; see Chapter IV.D for affected text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign Financial Disclosure reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with Section 10339B (Foreign Financial Support) of the CHIPS and Science Act (42 U.S.C. § 19040), each 'recipient institution of higher education' must annually report all current financial support of $50,000 or more (including gifts and contracts) received directly or indirectly from a foreign source that is associated with a foreign country of concern; requirement applies only to direct recipients of NSF funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies definitions, reporting of tuition, report due dates, and information collection use. Determination of 'direct recipient' is based on the entity receiving NSF awards through its own UEI; satellite/branch/regional campuses that are not direct recipients must report via the main campus. Excludes entities receiving only subawards and individuals who are beneficiaries of awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial requirements and electronic payments modernization
rubrics_metrics.description: Revised for compliance with Executive Order 14247 to require electronic remittances; references to routine check remittances removed. Checks are allowed only when electronic remittances are not practical and only under extraordinary or rare circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides NSF contact information for exceptions. Award ID(s) and reason for return must be included in any remittance. The only exception to prompt refunding is when funds will be disbursed immediately; exceptions considered case-by-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program income management and remittance procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Efforts should be made to avoid unexpended program income at grant end; program income earned during the project period should be expended prior to requesting reimbursement. If unexpended program income remains at the end of the grant, it must be remitted to NSF by crediting costs otherwise chargeable or, if not possible, remitted electronically or by check payable to the National Science Foundation via Pay.gov or Credit Gateway.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References ACM$ recording; directs use of Pay.gov or Treasury Credit Gateway and cross-references payment exceptions described in VIII.D.2. Contact Division of Financial Management for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Security assessments, documentation, and training requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds Research Security Assessment and Required Recipient Documentation requirements; recipients must maintain supporting documentation and meet Research Security Training Requirements specified in sections 10337 and 10634 of the CHIPS and Science Act of 2022 (42 U.S.C. §§ 1862o-1, 19040).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed requirements are provided in NSF Important Notice 149 (sections 1 and 2) issued July 10, 2025. These requirements supersede existing guidance in PAPPG 24-1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment unit acquisition threshold increase
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with 2 CFR § 200.313(e), NSF may identify items of equipment having a unit acquisition cost of $10,000 or more (increased from $5,000) where NSF reserves the right to transfer title to the Federal government or a named third party at any time during the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aligns NSF equipment threshold with Title 2 CFR updates; impacts property title and transfer rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property management requirements for Federally Owned Property (FOP) and inventory reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: When title to equipment or real property is vested in the Federal government, such FOP must be identified/tagged or segregated to indicate Federal ownership, used only for project performance (unless award provides otherwise), and reported via annual and final inventory reports by NSF award number to NSF's Central Property Inventory Repository (CPIR). A physical inventory of FOP must be conducted every two years and the annual report must be received in CPIR no later than Oct. 15 each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual inventory reporting requirement applies to FOP with original acquisition cost of $10,000 or more (per 2 CFR § 200.312(a)). Report content must include: description of property; serial/ID number; funding source (including FAIN); title holder; acquisition date; cost; percentage of Federal contribution; location/use/condition; disposition data (date of disposal and sale price); and description of Construction-in-Progress (CIP) and Work-in-Progress (WIP) and costs. Final inventory report due at award end and must include disposition request. OMB-approved SF-428 series forms may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific integrity alignment with Gold Standards of Science
rubrics_metrics.description: Chapter XI.M is revised to align NSF scientific integrity language with NSF Gold Standards of Science; previous text emphasizing inclusivity, transparency, and protection from inappropriate influence has been struck.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals an update in how scientific integrity principles are expressed in the PAPPG; cross-reference to Gold Standard Science Implementation Plan. The revision removes specific prior phrasing while maintaining focus on integrity-related principles as updated by NSF policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research misconduct definition expanded to include AI-based tools
rubrics_metrics.description: RESEARCH MISCONDUCT is defined to mean fabrication, falsification, or plagiarism whether committed directly or through the use or assistance of other persons, entities, or tools, including artificial intelligence (AI)-based tools, in proposing or performing research funded by NSF, reviewing research proposals submitted to NSF, or in reporting NSF-funded research results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly incorporates AI-based tools into the scope of potential research misconduct; applies to research proposal preparation, review, and reporting activities funded by NSF.
